Amazon (AMZN +0.81%) reported its first-quarter 2026 earnings on April 29, 2026, and the results were generally strong. Revenue and earnings both exceeded analysts' expectations, and the company's cost-cutting efforts drove excellent profit margin growth.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) was an especially strong point, with revenue up 28% year over year, accelerating from the previous rate. Amazon's operating margin hit an all-time high of 13.1% in the quarter. [...] 18.85%

In the first quarter of 2026, Tesla (TSLA +2.83%) reported a 16% year-over-year increase in revenue, and adjusted EPS significantly beat expectations thanks to the strongest gross margin Tesla has produced in five quarters. Looking ahead, the company is focusing on robotics, automation, and other futuristic products, with Model S production ending and its factory being converted for robotics production. [...] 0.24%

In the first quarter of 2026, Alphabet (GOOG -0.88%) (GOOGL -0.96%) (better known for its main subsidiary, Google) reported both revenue and earnings that exceeded analysts' expectations. The company reported nearly $110 billion in revenue, up 22% year-over-year, an impressive growth rate for such a massive business.

For the full year 2026, analysts expect S&P 500 earnings to increase by 18.9%. Edward Yardeni, a well-respected market and economic analyst, says those growth expectations may be too bullish and that analysts may be entering the realm of irrational exuberance. Yardeni adds that a major risk is that some of the big AI data center companies like Meta Platforms and Alphabet don't beat analysts' overly optimistic earnings growth estimates, which could cause a correction among technology stocks. [...] Expectations are high for Q2 earnings reports from several major companies.

ByMatthew Benjamin – Jul 9, 2026 at 1:53PM EST

+Fool.comon

## Key Points

 Analysts expect S&P 500 earnings to grow 23.3% year over year in Q2.
 One analyst says the consensus estimates might be too optimistic.

Net sales rose 5.2% as adjusted EPS jumped 53% on wholesale strength.
